BASIC - Test horizontal privilege escalation: log in as a standard user and attempt to access admin endpoints by directly calling admin-only API routes (/api/admin/users, /api/admin/settings) without an admin session
BASIC - Test whether admin functions (user deletion, role assignment, config changes) are protected by CSRF tokens; a CSRF attack against admin actions can have catastrophic consequences
INTERMEDIATE - Test admin panel for IDOR: as an admin managing your own tenant, modify resource identifiers to access or manage another tenant's users, settings, or data

INTERMEDIATE - Test whether admin audit logs are complete, tamper-proof, and capture all sensitive actions (user deletion, permission changes, data exports, config modifications); attempt to perform an action and verify it appears in the audit log

INTERMEDIATE - Test admin impersonation features: if the admin panel allows impersonating a user account, verify the impersonated session is clearly flagged and that the admin cannot perform actions that bypass the impersonated user's permissions
INTERMEDIATE - Test bulk action endpoints in admin panels: bulk delete, bulk export, or bulk status change endpoints often have weaker per-record permission checks than individual record actions

ADVANCED - Test for second-order XSS via admin panel: inject a payload into a user-submitted field (username, address, description) that is stored and later rendered in the admin panel without sanitisation, executing in the admin's browser context

ADVANCED - Test admin panel for mass assignment: send an API request to an admin user-update endpoint with additional fields not shown in the UI (is_superadmin, can_delete_tenants, billing_exempt) and verify the server rejects undeclared fields

sections.title: Page-Specific Testing - Checkout & Payment Page
items: BASIC - Test whether the payment amount shown in the UI is independently re-calculated server-side at the time of payment, or whether a client-supplied total is trusted; intercept the checkout POST and modify the amount field

BASIC - Test for PCI DSS scope: identify whether the application handles raw card numbers directly or offloads card entry to a third-party gateway iframe; if the app handles card data directly (SAQ D scope), verify TLS, tokenisation, and no card data logging

BASIC - Test the address verification flow: submit a billing address that does not match the card's registered address (AVS mismatch) and verify the application handles the AVS failure gracefully without leaking the card's actual registered address

INTERMEDIATE - Test for currency confusion: if the payment supports multiple currencies, switch currency mid-session and verify the price is correctly recalculated; test whether currency codes can be set to invalid values (e.g., XXX) that result in zero amounts

INTERMEDIATE - Test for 3DS (3D Secure) bypass: determine whether 3DS authentication can be skipped by directly calling the order confirmation endpoint after the initial payment intent is created, without completing the 3DS challenge

INTERMEDIATE - Test payment retry logic: if a payment fails (card declined), verify the retry does not charge the card for the original amount twice; also test whether a failed payment leaves an inventory reservation in place indefinitely

ADVANCED - Test for payment gateway callback validation: the payment gateway sends a server-to-server callback (webhook) to confirm payment; test whether replaying this callback, or forging it without a valid signature, marks an order as paid

ADVANCED - Test for open redirect in the payment return URL: if the post-payment redirect URL is user-controlled or stored in the session, test whether it can be manipulated to redirect users to a phishing page after a legitimate payment

sections.title: Advanced Supplement - Authentication (Additions)
items: ADVANCED - Test credential stuffing resilience: use a known breached credential list (email:password combos) against the login endpoint and verify the application detects and blocks credential stuffing based on velocity, device fingerprint, or IP reputation

ADVANCED - Test password spraying resistance: attempt login with a single common password (Password1!) across a large number of valid usernames; unlike brute force this avoids per-account lockout thresholds
ADVANCED - Test for authentication bypass via HTTP verb tampering: send the login POST as a GET, PUT, or HEAD request and verify the server does not process credentials on unexpected HTTP methods

ADVANCED - Test JWT token security on authenticated endpoints: decode the JWT, change the algorithm to none (alg:none attack), and re-submit without a signature; verify the server rejects unsigned tokens

ADVANCED - Test for authentication logic bypass via null/empty values: submit login requests with username=null, password=[], or missing required fields and verify the server returns an auth error rather than authenticating as an anonymous or default user

ADVANCED - Test biometric/passwordless authentication flows: if the application supports WebAuthn/FIDO2, verify that the challenge is unique per-authentication, expires quickly, and is validated server-side rather than client-side

sections.title: Advanced Supplement - Session Management (Additions)
items: ADVANCED - Test for session token entropy: collect 50+ session tokens and analyse them with Burp Sequencer; tokens with insufficient entropy can be predicted or guessed

ADVANCED - Test session token binding: capture a session token from one IP and attempt to reuse it from a different IP and user agent; well-implemented session binding should detect and reject the re-used token

ADVANCED - Test for cookie-based session fixation: manually set a session cookie in the browser before logging in and verify the server replaces it with a new token after authentication rather than elevating the attacker-supplied cookie to an authenticated state

ADVANCED - Test session persistence after privilege change: elevate a user account to admin in one tab; in another tab using the same session, verify the elevated permissions are immediately reflected rather than requiring a new login

ADVANCED - Test for cross-subdomain session leakage: if the session cookie's domain attribute is set to .domain.com (with leading dot), verify that a subdomain (e.g., attacker-controlled.domain.com) cannot read and steal the session cookie

sections.title: Advanced Supplement - Input Validation (Additions)
items: ADVANCED - Test for template injection (SSTI): inject {{7*7}}, ${7*7}, or <%= 7*7 %> into any input that might be rendered by a server-side template engine (Jinja2, Twig, Freemarker, Velocity); if the response contains 49, SSTI is present and RCE is likely

ADVANCED - Test for prototype pollution in JavaScript-heavy applications: submit JSON payloads containing __proto__ or constructor.prototype keys and verify the server sanitises these before merging into application objects

ADVANCED - Test for mass assignment / auto-binding vulnerabilities: submit API requests containing additional fields not exposed in the application UI (is_admin, role, balance, email_verified) and verify the server ignores undeclared fields rather than binding them

ADVANCED - Test for ReDoS (Regular Expression Denial of Service): identify input fields that use regex validation and submit inputs crafted to trigger catastrophic backtracking (e.g., a long string of 'aaa...a!' against a regex like ^(a+)+$); measure response time degradation

ADVANCED - Test for HTTP request smuggling on input fields: submit requests with both Transfer-Encoding: chunked and Content-Length headers to check whether front-end and back-end servers disagree on request boundaries, enabling request smuggling

sections.title: Advanced Supplement - API Security (Additions)
items: ADVANCED - Test for BOLA (Broken Object Level Authorisation) systematically: for every API endpoint that accepts an object ID in the URL or body, test whether substituting another user's object ID returns or modifies their data

ADVANCED - Test for BFLA (Broken Function Level Authorisation): map all API endpoints using the application as a regular user, then replay each request with a lower-privilege token (or no token) to identify functions that fail to enforce role checks

ADVANCED - Test for API versioning security regression: if the application has /api/v1/ and /api/v2/ endpoints, test whether the older version (v1) enforces the same security controls as v2; old versions are often left behind with weaker authentication or missing rate limiting

ADVANCED - Test for excessive data exposure in API responses: compare what the API returns with what the UI actually displays; if the API returns 50 fields but the UI shows 5, the remaining 45 fields (which may include PII, internal IDs, or sensitive flags) are still accessible to any client

ADVANCED - Test for API key scope enforcement: if the application issues API keys with defined scopes (read-only, write, admin), test whether a read-only key can perform write operations by directly calling write endpoints

ADVANCED - Test for mass assignment in API PUT/PATCH endpoints: send a PUT or PATCH request with additional JSON fields beyond those documented (e.g., add is_verified:true, subscription:premium) and verify the server only updates the permitted fields
